fragments.text: My name is David Tiam and I'm the director for the African Open Science Platform. We're very excited to be part of this years conference, particularly to share what we are doing in the continent through the African Open Science Platform in advancing forest open science, but haven't used for AI in the continent. There's very clear use cases, good examples of the use of AI in terms of various domains. But I think it's very critical to look at the building blocks that will enable the continent, for example, to be able to accrue the best on the ground of AI. There's clearly a lack of enabling policies that will provide the SCAR funding for developing AI in the continent.

fragments.text: We have done significant work to date in terms of policy influence, very few countries have got open science policies. Only Ethiopia has got a ratified policy. South Africa is going through the motions of consulting with policy and also taking it to cabinet and relevant structures. But by and large, both countries are still at the end stages. ASP engages with regional blocks such as Sadek to collect real advance areas of open science policy development. And we also do a lot of studies. We're also currently looking at a study regarding open science and geoinformatics to look at the potential for geoinformatics in space sciences. You can agree that space science provides a very, very good opportunity for socio economic development in the continent.
